source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.3.4 Balancing Parentheses (PDF 99, printed 96). Short question 4 is answered.

items: Use a stack to keep track of opening parentheses.
On an opening parenthesis, push it.
On a closing parenthesis, pop the top of the stack.
If the stack is empty at the end, the parentheses are balanced.
If the stack is not empty, or a pop is tried on an empty stack, they are not balanced.

blocks.text: Example: (3 + 4) * (5 - 2) is balanced: each ( has a matching ).

blocks.prompt: How does a stack help balance parentheses (short question 4)? Check (a + b)) * (c.
blocks.explanation: Push each ( and pop for each ); the expression is balanced only if no pop meets an empty stack and the stack is empty at the end. In (a + b)) * (c the second ) tries to pop an empty stack, so it is not balanced.

items: Push '(', pop on ')'; balanced if never popping an empty stack and empty at the end.
